title: Click a booster seat's tray onto both armrests at its second notch
instruction: Put the tray on the booster seat at its middle setting, locked at the second notch.
context: Parents and childcare workers put a toddler's feeding tray on a booster seat or high chair at every meal, at the setting that fits the child: the middle notch leaves about 12 cm between the tray and the backrest. Unlike sliding one carriage until it clicks, both catches, 36 cm apart, must drop into the same notch, and the push has to stop inside a 25 mm window against about 12 N of clicks, on a seat that stands free on its feet.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Booster seat (white moulded polypropylene shell, 40 cm wide (y) x 33 cm deep (x) x 23 cm tall, 2.5 kg, on four 4 x 4 cm black rubber feet, chair straps tucked under), facing the robot, its front face at x = 0.455, centred on y = 0: a low seat shell whose seat surface is 3 cm above the table; a backrest 4 cm thick at the far end; two armrests 4 cm wide (|y| from 0.135 to 0.175), 12 cm above the seat (top 15 cm above the table), running from 3 cm to 29 cm behind the front face, the top front edge chamfered 1.5 cm at 45 degrees. On each armrest's outer face is a light-blue rack (acetal): three teeth 8 mm deep at 25 mm pitch, each 16 mm long at the root with a 45-degree ramp facing the front and a square back face, the first ramp starting 10 cm behind the front face; a square stop 2 cm deep behind the third notch (from 17.5 cm); and an 8 mm lip along the top from 7.5 cm behind the front face (1 cm tall, flush with the armrest top) that closes the notches from above. Teeth and stop span heights 11 to 14 cm. Notch 1, 2 and 3 are the gaps behind the first, second and third tooth. Tray (orange rigid polypropylene, 42 cm wide x 25 cm deep, 6 mm plate, 0.45 kg): a front rim 4 mm thick, 3 cm tall; 2 cm side rims; under the plate two rail walls (5 mm thick, 3.2 cm deep, 22 cm long) that pass just inside the armrests with 1.5 mm clearance, and an outer skirt at each end. In each tray end is a catch (dark grey acetal slide with a round 8 mm nose, 1.4 cm tall, 20 g) 10 cm behind the tray's centre, sprung inward (0.6 N/mm, 10 mm travel; about 12 N in all to click the tray over a tooth) so its tip sits 2 mm off the armrest face (6 mm into a notch), 1.7 to 3.1 cm below the plate; a 1.6 cm lug sticks out of the tray end to pull it out by hand. Start: the tray lies flat on the table on its rails and skirts, right side up, front rim toward the robot, centred on y = 0 with its back edge 5 mm in front of the booster's front face (tray centre at x = 0.325). Seated at notch 1, 2 or 3, the tray's back edge is 14.5, 12 or 9.5 cm from the backrest.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a photo during the trial. 0 if at any time the booster is moved more than 3 cm or tipped more than 10 degrees, the tray falls (drops faster than 0.6 m/s, about a 2 cm fall, while no gripper holds it: every gripper point at least 2 cm from it), or anything falls off the table. A catch is locked in a notch when it has dropped in (its tip within 4 mm of the notch floor, half the 8 mm notch depth, as seen from below) with the tray resting flat on the armrests (plate within 5 mm of their tops, tilted under 5 degrees, centred within 6 mm). The notch is told by the tray's front edge: 10.5, 8 or 5.5 cm past the booster's front face for notch 1, 2 or 3. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 (success, held for 1 s) both catches locked in notch 2, both grippers' TCPs, pad tips and finger links at least 2 cm from the tray, and the tray and both arms still (tray under 1 cm/s, grippers under 2 cm/s); 0.75 both catches locked in notch 2 but the tray still held or moving; 0.5 both catches locked in notch 1 or both in notch 3; 0.25 the tray resting flat on both armrests, rails over them by at least 3 cm, let go (the same 2 cm test) but not locked; else 0. Doing nothing or refusing scores 0.
reset_notes: Pull both catch lugs outward together (or squeeze them toward each other's ends) and slide the tray off toward the robot; lay it flat at its start position. Check the booster's feet are on their marked outline.
fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes; ramps are boxes turned 45 degrees, catch noses cylinders. Each catch is a prismatic joint with a 600 N/m spring drive, no preload; teeth, lip and stop hold the tray by contact. Friction: catch 0.2, tray 0.4, feet 0.9. The seat stands unstrapped, as before it is strapped to a chair; the 3 cm move limit stands for the straps. No force limits or plastic flex simulated.
